summary: I built a small Python identity-resolution sample that demonstrates seeding synthetic profiles (with embeddings), creating a vector (HNSW) index, a match agent that performs vector KNN search, a merge agent that consolidates candidate profiles (LLM-assisted when API key present; rule-based fallback when not), an audit agent that records merges, and an orchestrator that writes golden records and audit entries back to the provided Azure DocumentDB database. I verified dependency installation, unit test, seeding, index creation, and an end-to-end run of the orchestrator writing golden records and audit entries to the live cluster. The sample reads the cluster connection string from DOCUMENTDB_URI and the LLM/embedding keys from OPENAI_* env vars (with a safe synthetic-embedding fallback when the key is not present).
how_to_run:
1) pip install -r requirements.txt
2) Set DOCUMENTDB_URI in your environment (required). Optionally set OPENAI_API_KEY (and OPENAI_EMBEDDING_MODEL/OPENAI_API_MODEL) to enable real embeddings and LLM merges. (See .env.example.)
3) python -m src.seed_data --n 200   # seeds data and attempts to create the vector index
4) python -m src.run_orchestrator --sample-size 10  # runs the orchestrator over a subset of profiles and writes golden records + audits
5) pytest  # runs a small unit test (fast)

Notes: secrets must come from environment variables. The seed script will synthesize embeddings if OPENAI_API_KEY is not set so you can run the sample end-to-end without an LLM account.

For a production-quality sample, update Beanie/Motor usage or Beanie version compatibility for the target cluster (or call init_beanie with an explicit MotorDatabase wrapper if required).

MCP tool returned an error when listing documents from 'merge_audits' (documentdb_find_documents). The collection exists and contains audit entries (confirmed by the orchestrator run and by documentdb_list_databases), but the MCP 'find documents' call failed for that collection in this run. Investigate MCP server logs or retry the query if detailed inspection of audit entries via the MCP tool is required.

LLM integration cannot be verified without an OPENAI_API_KEY. The sample includes a safe synthetic-embedding and rule-based merge fallback so functionality can be demonstrated without a key, but to validate LLM-assisted merging and real embeddings you must set OPENAI_API_KEY and optionally OPENAI_EMBEDDING_MODEL/OPENAI_API_MODEL in the environment.
